executive_summary: This assessment reviewed the Parcelworks platform from its supplied overview — four zones and nineteen components — and approved two findings, described below. What could not be determined from the document is recorded as documentation gaps rather than concluded.
system_overview: The platform books and tracks parcel shipments: customers and drivers enter through gateways at the edge, a set of core services owns orders, routing, dispatch, tracking, notifications, labels, and billing over a message bus and data stores, carrier partners connect through an operations-zone link, and interactive sign-in is delegated to the company SSO provider, as the supplied document describes.
risk_summary: The approved findings concern the admin console being reached through the same sign-in path customers use while holding read-and-edit reach over every customer account, and notification templates logging full message bodies — names, addresses, and delivery windows — to the shared application log. The open items are the unwritten retention of the warehouse's nightly copies and the unstated enforcement of the data zone's reachability, both recorded as documentation gaps.

limitations.text: fnd-001 rests on stated assumptions: No common false positive applies: the console's access path is documented as the same SSO accounts and same sign-in path customers use, which is not a stronger path — the conclusion rests on that statement, not on an absent role-based permission matrix or absent operator-onboarding description, which the catalog names as false positives.

fnd-002 rests on stated assumptions: No common false positive applies: full message bodies are documented as logged, which is not an absent field-level redaction list where identifier-only logging is documented, nor an absent retention period — the false positives the catalog names.
